London, 16<sup>th</sup> March 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**U.S. President Barack Obama’s administration** added bankruptcy lawyer Matthew Feldman to the auto industry team advising the government on the restructuring of General Motors Corp. and Chrysler LLC.  Feldman, a partner at New York-based Willkie Farr & Gallagher LLP, joins other experts aiding government officials as the automakers use up an initial $17.4 billion in federal assistance. The U.S. Treasury Department last month hired law firms Cadwalader, Wickersham & Taft LLP and Sonnenschein, Nath & Rosenthal, as well as Rothschild Inc., an investment bank.  Feldman will work on restructuring analysis, said an administration official.  “We’re pleased that the task force is staffing up,” GM Chief Financial Officer Ray Young said in an interview. “They aren’t just looking at General Motors. They’re looking at the total industry. It shows that they’re taking this assignment very seriously.” _Source:  Automotive News_ 

**Toyota** will halt production at its Russian factory between March 30 and April 6. The plant, opened in 2007 to produce 20,000 Toyota Camry vehicles/year and cost 5 billion roubles ($141.7 million) to build. A collapse in the Russia car market deepened last month with sales down 38% y-o-y after a 33 % fall in January. Toyota’s sales was even more severe, falling 43% in February y-oy. Analysts expect the market to decline by 40 to 50% in 2009. Most of Toyota’s peers in Russia have also idled their assembly lines in the past four months, with Russia’s Kamaz imposing four suspensions since November. _Source:  Reuters_ 

**LG Display** has commenced mass production of its 8th generation LCD plant in Paju, Korea.  The 8th generation LCD line will primarily manufacture 32-, 47- and 55inch TV panels from its 2,200mm X 2,500mm glass substrates. LG Display invested KRW2,535 billion in the line, excluding the building cost. With initial monthly capacity of 20,000 input sheets of glass substrate, LG Display will adjust the rampup speed according to market circumstances and gradually increase monthly capacity to design capacity of 83,000 sheets by year-end.  The start of mass production in the 8th generation plant will enable LG Display to respond to growing market demand further stimulated by narrowed price gap between LCD TV and CRT TV and the rapidly increasing China market, thanks to the Chinese government’s “Home Appliances to the Countryside” policy.  According to DisplaySearch, the fast-growing LCD TV market will reach 181 million units in 2011, up 35 %from the 134 million units expected for this year. _Source:  EE Times Asia_ 

**Sylvania Resources** announced it is fast-tracking the development of its new Doornbosch and Tweefontein chrome and platinum recovery plants.  Construction on Doornbosch started in January, with commissioning now set for June, four months earlier than the initially planned commissioning date of January 2010. The plant would produce abo

ut 26koz/y of platinum-group metals (PGMs). The Tweefontein plant would now be commissioned by the end of this year, with construction to start this month. Production of 4E (platinum, palladium, rhodium and gold) PGMs increased to 13 124 oz during the six months ended December 31, 2008, compared with 5 621 oz in the six months ended December 2007. The company had been able to maintain production despite cutbacks by its key supplier of feed for its plants, Samancor Chrome, which had shut all its mining and smelting operations from mid-December to endFebruary.  Meanwhile, construction on the A$23-million Lannex PGMs plant would be completed by March. _Source:  Mining Weekly_ 

**Chromex Mining Plc** said it received mining rights for platinum group metals and gold at Stellite chrome project on the western limb of the Bushveld complex in South Africa.  Chromex said it would conduct a series of tests on the tailing streams to determine the economics of adding a PGE flotation treatment plant to the gravity concentration plant currently under construction. _Source:  Reuters_
